tagline.text: A clear river that supplies the island's water and power, and a cliff-jumping spot

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱200–1,000 (per person, local transport and meals only, excluding travel to the island)

children.text: The Cantingas River is a clear river in Taclobo, San Fernando, on Sibuyan Island. It is known for cliff jumping from multi-level diving platforms and for swimming, and it also serves the island's drinking water and hydropower.

The Cantingas River is in Barangay Taclobo in the municipality of San Fernando, in the southeast of Sibuyan Island in Romblon province. Sibuyan is called the "Galapagos of Asia," and Mount Guiting-Guiting rises in the middle of the island, with water running down from around the mountain forming clear rivers and waterfalls. The Cantingas is the most visited of these, and it is only 10–15 minutes by tricycle from the center of San Fernando. One travel blog says the riverside resort is about
4 km
from the town and about
off the main road.

The river's greatest pride is how clean its water is. Wikipedia reports that the Cantingas River was named the cleanest and greenest river in the Philippines in 2003 and 2005, and describes the water as odorless, tasteless and cold. One blog says the river is the drinking water source for island residents. The same post says a small hydropower plant near the river produces up to about 900 kW, supplies about 90 percent of the island's electricity and has served roughly 57,000 users since 2010. These figures come from a single blog, so confirm exact numbers locally.

For visitors, the concrete diving platforms are the symbol of the place. They come in three levels, bottom, middle and top, so you can jump from a height that suits you, and one traveler wrote that the water was deeper than about 2.4 m (8 ft) in some spots. The same person said it was shallower than before and partly dammed, so check the depth yourself before jumping. Weekends bring many families, while weekday mornings are quiet. It is a stretch to come all the way to Sibuyan Island just for the Cantingas River. Getting here from Manila takes a full day by boat, and the island has no scheduled airport. So most travelers combine it with places such as Mount Guiting-Guiting, Cresta de Gallo island and Lambingan Falls and plan two or three days. Of those, the Cantingas River is the least demanding stop. It is a good place to cool off after a climb, or to visit on the afternoon you arrive. Admission and facilities can change, so treat the prices here as checked in 2026 and follow local notices. Several waterfalls on Sibuyan are also mentioned in guides. Lambingan Falls in Magdiwang is a small fall you can visit without a guide, while Cataja Falls takes more than an hour to climb to the top and requires a guide. If you love swimming, you can spend one day each on the river and the falls without getting bored.

The concrete diving platforms are divided into bottom, middle and top levels. Start from a low level, check the depth and then work your way up. The platform heights were not given in the sources, so I could not confirm them.
Wikipedia says the water is odorless, tasteless and cold. Just dipping your feet at the water's edge takes the heat away, and there are pools suited to swimming with a group.
It is said to have been named the cleanest and greenest river in the Philippines in 2003 and 2005. Other guides do not name the award, so confirm the name locally.

The river is also used as drinking water for island residents, and a small hydropower plant nearby is said to supply the island's electricity. Do not use soap or detergent so you do not pollute the water.

At the river entrance there is a facility with cottages and a conference hall, and one blog says the facilities are limited to paved paths and diving platforms, so the natural feel remains. Confirm the details of the facilities locally.
Wikipedia says Lagting Falls, about
3 km
from the town, is in the same Barangay Taclobo. Visit it too if you have time. San Fernando also has Busay Falls in Panangcalan (about
2.5 km
from the town) and Dagubdob Falls in Olango, with several tiers of pools.

blocks.title: At the foot of Mount Guiting-Guiting

children.text: San Fernando is the municipality with the southern trailhead of Mount Guiting-Guiting. Resting at the Cantingas River after a climb fits naturally into the plan.

items.title: Half-day plan
items.subtitle: Swimming and jumping at the river

children.text: Set out from San Fernando town to the Cantingas River by tricycle. Weekday mornings are quiet.
Pay the entrance fee and look around the diving platforms and the swimming area.
Check the depth, then try jumping from the low level first and enjoy swimming in the clear water.
Have lunch with a packed meal or snacks in the shade and rest.
Return to town for a meal, and in the afternoon visit other waterfalls or the port area.
On days with frequent showers the water level can rise, so judge by the weather and the state of the river.

items.title: Full-day plan
items.subtitle: A tour of San Fernando's waters

children.text: Have breakfast at your lodging and head to the Cantingas River.
Stop at nearby water spots such as Lagting Falls by tricycle.
After lunch, check the boat to Cresta de Gallo island at San Fernando port.
Enjoy the sandbar and sea on the island and return before dark.
Return to town to watch the sunset and have dinner.
Take a bus from Manila to Batangas Port. One guide gives the fare as about ₱150–270.
From Batangas, board the Starlite ferry to Ambulong Port (Magdiwang) on Sibuyan Island. A 2023 guide gave a
departure (Monday–Saturday), about
9–10 hours
and about ₱1,250, while a 2026 guide gave about
12 hours
and ₱700–1,000, so check the latest schedule.
There is also a Starhorse ferry from Lucena (Dalahican), reported to take about
16 hours
Sailing days and times change. Check the operator's latest notice.

items.title: From Ambulong Port to San Fernando

children.text: From Ambulong Port (Magdiwang) to San Fernando is reported at about
1–2 hours
by jeepney. The road is rough, so allow extra time.
From San Fernando town to the Cantingas River is about
10–15 minutes
by tricycle.
One guide put a 20-minute tricycle ride at about $2–3, but fares vary with bargaining and season, so confirm locally.
Sibuyan Island has no scheduled airport. The nearest airport with air service is Tugdan Airport (TBH) on Tablas Island.
Boats run to Sibuyan Island from Romblon Island and from Roxas (Panay). One travel guide says the Romblon–Sibuyan route often sails once a day, in the morning.

Swimming and cliff jumping are best in the drier season. Sibuyan has no sharply defined wet and dry seasons, but rain is generally heaviest from June to November, and January to May is closer to a dry season. Right after rain the water level rises and the water can turn cloudy.
Weekday mornings are the quietest part of the day. Weekends bring many families, so choose your time accordingly.

One guide says Mount Guiting-Guiting is best climbed in February–May, with climbing restricted in November–January. If you want to combine the climb with the Cantingas River, planning it for February–May is easier.

Lodging is in San Fernando town and on the Magdiwang side. A travel blog said Seabreeze Inn in San Fernando costs about ₱800 a night for an air-conditioned double, and Magdiwang has guesthouses and small resorts. That information is from 2019, so names and rates may have changed. Check on a booking site.

You will eat at small restaurants and the market in town. I could not confirm whether there are restaurants at the river, so bring water, snacks and lunch. Mobile signal on Sibuyan is weak, so download any maps you need in advance. Carry plenty of cash.

According to Wikipedia, San Fernando had a population of about 23,600 in the 2024 census, making it the third most populous town in Romblon province. It began in 1636 as a small village called Cauit in Azagra, was renamed in 1882 and became a municipality on January 1, 1947. In town, tricycles and jeepneys gather when ships arrive, and pumpboats from the port run to Roxas and Romblon Island.
Weekday mornings are the quietest and photos come out well.
Check the depth with your own eyes before you jump, and start at a low level.
Bring swimwear, shoes that can get wet, a towel and a waterproof pouch.
The river is a drinking water source, so do not use soap or shampoo, and take your trash with you.
Bargain with your tricycle driver for a round trip including waiting time.
Right after rain the water can rise and be dangerous, so check the water level.
Combine the river with a climb of Mount Guiting-Guiting or a trip to Cresta de Gallo island for a fuller Sibuyan visit.
Mobile signal is weak, so save maps and your itinerary in advance.
When touring the island, consider adding Lambingan Falls (in Silum, Magdiwang, reported as 10–15 minutes from town by car), Ipil Point, a sunset spot facing the sea, and Azagra Lighthouse Hill.
Wikipedia says tricycles and jeepneys run around town and the island, so ask your lodging in advance about a day-charter rate.
The depth for cliff jumping is not uniform and can change with dam work. Always check the depth yourself before you jump.
I could not confirm the platform heights or safety rules. Follow local guidance on the diving platforms.
When it rains the water level can rise and the current can speed up, so do not enter the water on bad-weather days.
I could not confirm whether lifeguards are present, so keep children within arm's reach.
Mobile signal is weak on the island and emergency medical facilities are far away. Carry a personal first-aid kit.
The entrance fee and facility information mixes sources from 2019 to 2026 and may differ from the present.
Even if the water looks clear, do not swallow it while swimming, and do not stay in the water for long if you have a wound.
